clue.text: Hot climate is pointless for hardy plant

indicators.note: a point is a compass point, so the word for climate loses its West

parts.note: weather stands in loosely for climate here

explanation.surface: A tough shrub is said not to care about a hot climate.
explanation.walkthrough: In crosswords a 'point' is one of the compass points N, E, S or W.
explanation.definitionFit: Heather is a low evergreen shrub that thrives on bleak moorland, so it is a hardy plant.

clue.text: Sweet murmur made by insect?

parts.note: a hum is a low continuous murmur
bug is the everyday word for any insect

explanation.surface: Asks whether a soft buzzing sound comes from an insect.
explanation.walkthrough: A humbug is a striped, mint-flavoured boiled sweet, familiar in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A humbug is a type of hard confectionery, so it is an example of a sweet.

clue.text: Commercial break has no clear purpose

definitions.note: a verb phrase standing for the adjective: someone adrift is without direction

parts.note: an ad is a television commercial
a rift is a break or split

explanation.surface: A television ad break seems to serve no real purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: To be adrift is to be aimless, drifting without any direction or goal.

clue.text: Late bishop had trouble being sociable

indicators.note: the words are troubled, that is disturbed, so their letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: the two words supply the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A deceased bishop struggled to mix with people.
explanation.definitionFit: A hospitable person is welcoming and friendly to guests, close in sense to sociable.

clue.text: Partially grow a new tree

indicators.note: only part of the run of words is used, so the answer lies within them

parts.note: the answer runs across the end of grow, all of a and the start of new

explanation.surface: An instruction to grow part of a new tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The rowan, or mountain ash, is a small tree with red berries.

clue.text: Cold compress to get rid of beginnings of muscle deficiency

definitions.meaning: the definition, and also read as cold plus compress

definitions.text: to get rid of beginnings of muscle deficiency
definitions.meaning: describes the use of the item: easing the first signs of a strained muscle

explanation.surface: A cold compress is applied to stop a muscle problem developing.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition doubles as a charade: cold gives ICE and compress gives PACK; the rest of the clue describes what the thing is for.
explanation.definitionFit: An ice pack is a bag of ice held against an injury, a type of cold compress.

clue.text: Loves working in pub, but finally ends with no money

indicators.note: the rearranged letters sit inside the word for pub

parts.note: an inn is a pub

indicators.note: the letters are put to work, that is worked into a new order

parts.note: the word supplies the letters to rearrange

indicators.note: only the last letter of but is used

parts.note: the last letter of but

explanation.surface: Someone who loves working in a pub still ends up broke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ends' is a link word here, joining the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An insolvent person or firm cannot pay its debts, being without funds.

clue.text: God has backache!

indicators.note: the back part of the single word backache says to read the word for ache in reverse

parts.note: to be sore is to ache

explanation.surface: A deity is complaining of a backache.
explanation.walkthrough: The single word backache splits into back, the reversal signal, and ache.
explanation.definitionFit: Eros is the Greek god of love, counterpart of Cupid.

clue.text: Sailor's old instrument is complete

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, with the possessive S
a lute is a stringed instrument

explanation.surface: A sailor's antique instrument is all there.
explanation.definitionFit: Absolute means total or utter, as in absolute silence, so complete.

clue.text: Favour shown by nice head

parts.note: kind and nice are near synonyms
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness or Sheerness

explanation.surface: A favour done by a pleasant boss.
explanation.walkthrough: NESS is a headland, a common crossword meaning of head.
explanation.definitionFit: A kindness is a kind act done for someone, much like a favour.

clue.text: Saint's stigmata?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: belonging to St Mark, the Gospel writer
second meaning: spots or scars, as the wounds of Christ appearing on a saint

explanation.walkthrough: The two readings are the possessive of the saint's name and the plural noun for spots or scars.
explanation.definitionFit: Stigmata are marks resembling Christ's wounds; the possessive of the evangelist's name is spelt identically.

clue.text: Not quite advisable to trick evil state

indicators.note: the word is not quite complete, so its last letter goes

parts.note: wise means sensible or advisable
to con is to trick
sin is wrongdoing, evil

explanation.surface: It would be unwise to fool an evil state.
explanation.definitionFit: Wisconsin is one of the fifty US states, in the Midwest.

clue.text: Red, funnily, turns out to mean cold!

indicators.note: the letters of the two words turn out differently, coming out in a new order

parts.note: both words supply the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Calling someone a Red, said as a joke, turns out to signal coolness towards them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'funnily' looks like the anagram signal but is part of the fodder; the signal is 'turns out'.
explanation.definitionFit: Cold in the sense of distant and unwelcoming, a manner lacking warmth or friendliness.

clue.text: Arrange for sleep over to include student

indicators.note: the reversed word takes the student letter inside it
over means turned over, so the word for sleep runs backwards

parts.note: a nap is a short sleep
L is the learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: Organising a sleepover that includes a student.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sleep over' reads as one word, sleepover, but splits into the nap and its reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To plan something is to arrange or organise it in advance.

clue.text: Backbone shown to improperly defy pro hunter

parts.note: split as back and bone: a rib is a bone, and back says to read it in reverse

indicators.note: the words are arranged improperly, out of their right order

parts.note: the two words supply the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Showing backbone means boldly defying a professional, though improperly.
explanation.walkthrough: Backbone is one word in the surface but splits into back, the reversal signal, and bone.
explanation.definitionFit: Hawks, eagles and falcons are birds of prey, hunting other animals for food.

clue.text: Is thankful when value goes up

definitions.meaning: first meaning: is grateful for something
second meaning: rises in value, as property does

explanation.surface: Someone is grateful when an asset rises in worth.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers both gratitude and an increase in an asset's worth, two separate senses.

clue.text: Elect syndicate in East Yorkshire town

indicators.note: the East letter goes inside the combined words

parts.note: to elect is to pick or choose
a ring is a group working together, such as a crime syndicate

explanation.surface: Choosing a business group in a town in East Yorkshire.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'East Yorkshire town', but East belongs to the wordplay; Pickering is in North Yorkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Pickering is a market town in Yorkshire, gateway to the North York Moors.

clue.text: Need second vehicle to go to town

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
a city is a large town

explanation.surface: Someone needs a second car to get into town.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarcity is shortage or want, close to need in the sense of lack.

clue.text: Famous Tamil revolutionary about to get memory back

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go about, that is around, the other piece
revolution means turning around, so the letters are turned into a new order

parts.note: the word supplies the letters to rearrange

indicators.note: back means the word for memory is reversed

parts.note: ROM is read-only memory in a computer

explanation.surface: A well-known Tamil rebel is about to recover his memory.
explanation.walkthrough: ROM, read-only memory, is a common crossword reading of memory.
explanation.definitionFit: An immortal reputation is one that lasts for ever, so the word is a stronger synonym of famous.

clue.text: Problematic company folded after market's opening

indicators.note: folded comes after the market letter
the opening of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of market
plicated is a technical word for folded or pleated

explanation.surface: A firm went under after trouble began at market.
explanation.walkthrough: PLICATED, folded, is a rare botanical and geological word.
explanation.definitionFit: A complicated matter is involved and difficult, therefore problematic.

clue.text: Bend over to put money in Delaware baby's cot

indicators.note: over means the word for bend is turned over and read backwards

parts.note: an arc is a bend or curve

indicators.note: the money letter goes inside the state abbreviation

parts.note: DE is the postal abbreviation for the US state
L is the pound sign, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: Someone stoops to put cash into a baby's cot in Delaware.
explanation.definitionFit: A cradle is a small bed for an infant, usually rocking, close to a cot.

clue.text: The rat represents a hazard

indicators.note: the letters re-present themselves, appearing again in a new order

parts.note: the two words supply the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: The rat poses a danger.
explanation.definitionFit: A threat is a source of possible danger, very close in meaning to hazard.

clue.text: Cause of tin man losing heart?

indicators.note: the robot is losing its heart, the middle letter

parts.note: a robot is a man made of metal, a tin man

explanation.surface: Wondering what is behind the Tin Man from Oz lacking a heart.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tin Man of The Wizard of Oz wanted a heart; here a robot loses its middle B.
explanation.definitionFit: The root of a problem is its underlying source or cause.

clue.text: Ron, the chef, is cooking from now on

indicators.note: cooking mixes the letters up, as a chef mixes ingredients

parts.note: the three words supply the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Ron the chef will be in the kitchen from now on.
explanation.definitionFit: Henceforth is a formal adverb meaning from this time forward.

clue.text: Knock down bloke in hat

definitions.note: an adjective here, as in knock-down prices

indicators.note: the bloke goes in the hat

parts.note: a cap is a kind of hat
he refers to any male, a bloke

explanation.surface: Someone flattens a man wearing a hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knock down' reads as a verb but is the adjective of bargain prices.
explanation.definitionFit: Knock-down prices are very low, so the goods are inexpensive.

clue.text: Left after outstanding contest

indicators.note: the left letter comes after the word for outstanding

parts.note: an outstanding payment is due

explanation.surface: Someone left after an excellent match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outstanding' looks like praise but means still owed.
explanation.definitionFit: A duel is a formal fight between two people, a contest of arms.

clue.text: Pushing in, I get book on new virus — first edition

parts.note: taken as written
NT is the New Testament, a book of the Bible

indicators.note: new means the letters are made into a new arrangement

parts.note: the word supplies the letters to rearrange

indicators.note: only the first letter of edition is taken

parts.note: the first letter of edition

explanation.surface: Someone barges in to get a book about a new virus in its first edition.
explanation.definitionFit: Intrusive means imposing oneself where not wanted, which is pushing in.

clue.text: Get lift, carrying note to bank

indicators.note: the word for get lift carries the note inside it

parts.note: to get a lift is to ride in someone's vehicle
G is a note of the musical scale

explanation.surface: Hitching a ride while carrying a banknote.
explanation.walkthrough: 'note' suggests money, matching 'bank', but it is the musical note G.
explanation.definitionFit: A ridge is a raised strip of ground, like a bank or long mound.

clue.text: Say you'll write in diary about the Christmas fire

indicators.note: say tells us to go by the sound of the word, not its spelling

parts.note: spoken aloud, you'll sounds like Yule, an old word for Christmas
to log is to record in a diary or journal

explanation.surface: An instruction to note in a diary something about the Christmas fire.
explanation.walkthrough: Yule is an old word for Christmas.
explanation.definitionFit: A Yule log is a large log traditionally burned in the hearth at Christmas.

clue.text: Allowance for young chaps taking part in strike

indicators.note: the young chaps take a part inside the word for strike

parts.note: to pat is to strike lightly
men are chaps

explanation.surface: An allowance for young men joining a strike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strike' suggests industrial action, but it is a light tap.
explanation.definitionFit: An allowance is a sum paid regularly to someone, so a payment.
